_llm_instructions: Populate the fields of 'SPRINT PLANNING LOG' and write the value of each field under 'Generated Value', based on the project context. Context: the project carrying reference PMO-04.03.10.

f01_Sprint_Goal.label: Sprint Goal
f01_Sprint_Goal.guidance: The one outcome the sprint is for, stated as a capability the team can demonstrate rather than as a list of stories. A goal written as a list of stories cannot be used to reject anything, and a sprint that cannot reject anything has no goal.

f02_Sprint_Window.label: Sprint Window
f02_Sprint_Window.guidance: The start and end dates, and the length of the sprint. The window is a constraint rather than a preference, because a sprint length that drifts produces a velocity figure that means nothing.

f03_Capacity_Basis.label: Capacity Basis
f03_Capacity_Basis.guidance: How much the team believes it can take on, and what that belief is based on. Capacity stated without its basis is a wish, and the first sprint is where a capacity figure is usually found to be wrong.

f04_Carry_over_From_the_Previous_Sprint.label: Carry-over From the Previous Sprint
f04_Carry_over_From_the_Previous_Sprint.guidance: What was not finished, and whether it has been re-estimated or carried as-is. Work carried without a new estimate is work whose estimate has never been tested.

f05_Story_ID.label: Story ID
f05_Story_ID.guidance: The identifier from the board, so the story can be traced when the sprint ends and the question is asked afterwards. A story with no identifier cannot be found again once it leaves the room.

f06_Story_Title.label: Story Title
f06_Story_Title.guidance: A short name for the story, in the language the team uses for it. A title that restates the acceptance criteria instead of naming the story makes the log harder to scan than the board it came from.

f07_Story_Points.label: Story Points
f07_Story_Points.guidance: The estimate for each story, and the scale used. Points are a relative comparison rather than a duration, so a scale changed between sprints makes two velocities incomparable.

f08_Priority.label: Priority
f08_Priority.guidance: Order relative to the other stories in this sprint, and why this story sits where it does. Priority stated as high or medium without a reason is a label rather than an ordering.

f09_Status.label: Status
f09_Status.guidance: Where the story stands at the end of the sprint, against what was committed. A status recorded only at review is too late to be useful to anyone planning the next sprint.

f10_Acceptance_Criteria.label: Acceptance Criteria
f10_Acceptance_Criteria.guidance: What will be true when the story is done, written so that a person who was not in the planning meeting can tell. Criteria agreed after the work is built describe whatever was built.

f11_Verified_By.label: Verified By
f11_Verified_By.guidance: Who checks the criteria and when. A criterion with no named verifier is a statement of intent, and the review becomes the first time anyone looks at it.

f12_Reason_Added.label: Reason Added
f12_Reason_Added.guidance: Why the story entered a sprint that had already been planned. The reason is the part worth recording, because it distinguishes a genuine discovery from a preference.

f13_Requested_By.label: Requested By
f13_Requested_By.guidance: Who asked for the addition, so the trade-off can be discussed with the person who wanted it. Scope added mid-sprint is how a sprint stops being a commitment.

f14_Effect_on_Sprint.label: Effect on Sprint
f14_Effect_on_Sprint.guidance: What the addition displaces, or which committed story now carries the risk of not finishing. An addition recorded without an effect reads as free, and it is not.

f15_Team_Member.label: Team Member
f15_Team_Member.guidance: The person, named rather than as a role, so the assignment can be checked against the person's actual availability.

f16_Role.label: Role
f16_Role.guidance: The role this person holds on the sprint, which is not the same as their title outside it. The role decides who settles an argument about scope during the sprint.

f17_Assigned_Stories.label: Assigned Stories
f17_Assigned_Stories.guidance: The stories this person is carrying in this sprint. The list is the thing to read for over-allocation: a person on every story in the log is a plan that has not been made yet.

f18_Available_Capacity.label: Available Capacity
f18_Available_Capacity.guidance: How much of this person's time the sprint actually has, after other commitments. Capacity at full for every story in the log is a statement of hope rather than of plan.

f19_Skill_and_Capacity_Gaps.label: Skill and Capacity Gaps
f19_Skill_and_Capacity_Gaps.guidance: What the committed scope needs that the team does not have. A gap named at planning is a risk to be managed; the same gap found at the end of the sprint is a surprise.

f20_Dependencies_Outside_the_Team.label: Dependencies Outside the Team
f20_Dependencies_Outside_the_Team.guidance: What must arrive from another team, and by when. A dependency with no date is an assumption, and it is usually discovered on the last day of the sprint.

f21_Risk.label: Risk
f21_Risk.guidance: What could stop the sprint, described as the event rather than as a feeling. A risk written as a concern cannot be managed, because there is nothing to watch for.

f22_Trigger.label: Trigger
f22_Trigger.guidance: The observable signal that the risk is happening. This is what makes a risk trackable: without a trigger the item is reviewed at the end of the sprint and found to have happened.

f23_Likelihood.label: Likelihood
f23_Likelihood.guidance: How likely the risk is, and what that judgement rests on. A bare high or low records no basis, so the next person cannot tell whether the estimate improved or the mood changed.

f24_Impact.label: Impact
f24_Impact.guidance: What the sprint loses if the risk occurs, measured in the same units as the commitment. Impact stated as severe is not comparable to a story estimate.

f25_Response.label: Response
f25_Response.guidance: What will be done about the risk while the sprint is running. A risk with no response is recorded in order to be mentioned later.

f26_Contingency.label: Contingency
f26_Contingency.guidance: What will be dropped or deferred if the risk occurs. A sprint with no contingency is a sprint where the decision gets made under pressure by whoever is most available at the time.
